all_segments.text: Nike is just about to release a pair of slides that could absolutely break the internet.
So this is the Nike React Rejuvenate slide. The amount of hype and anticipation for this pair of
shoes is so high, we really need to figure out if people are going to end up being disappointed
or not. So a couple of weeks ago, Nike released the React X Rejuvenate clog. And to my surprise,
people went absolutely crazy for these. They completely sold out in a bunch of different
colors and are actually reselling for over the retail price. From my point of view, before I
got these in, I wasn't really expecting much when I saw this pair of shoes, considering Nike and
Jordan Brand's track record of making not the most comfortable or even good looking slides and
clogs, most of those have been relatively underwhelming in terms of comfort and design.
But after testing these things out myself, the hype was real. So given how good these things were and
how hyped up they are, are these really going to stack up? Are they just as good? Are they better?
And how do they compare to other slides on the market? So first of all, let's go over how they
compare to the clocks. And yes, there is more differences than just Nike chopping the top off.
The first up price and release details. So these actually haven't fully released yet. They drop on
April the 23rd for $60 or 55 pounds. If you're here in the UK, these on the other hand released a few
weeks ago, like I said, they're always kind of restocking them, but they retail for $70 or 65 pounds.
If you're in the UK, both of these come with the exact same material. That's what's in the name,
React X. It's Nike's latest and one of their most premium cushionings that they have in a lot of
their flagship running shoes, like the Pegasus 41, the Plumero 18, and even the Pegasus Premium.
But unlike how the actual shoes just have a strip of it in the midsole, these things are completely
made out of the stuff. So right underneath your feet and also above your feet. And it's really
solid cushioning as far as comparatively to other brands and what they offer. It finds a great balance
of being soft and squishy without being unstable or something that just feels like marshmallows.
Obviously the design of these two is pretty much the same. They both have these lines or organic
grooves that wrap around the entire shoe. Funnily enough, they called these things rejuvenate,
which is named after the Air Rejuvenate, the original one from 2008, which was actually also
a recovery shoe. These just are obviously a little bit more geared towards the current style. You find the
exact same Nike logo on both of them, where it's like this rubbery gel-like material that's actually
glued into the side of the shoe. Obviously the clogs have a much larger version of that. They
shrunk it down for the slides. Both of these come with identical rubber traction patterns, which is
glued onto the bottom. This actually adds a lot of durability to the pair of shoes and is quite rare to
see in a foam clog or a foam pair of slides for that matter. A lot of the other ones on the market,
like any of the Yeezy slides, foam runners, or Crocs, those don't have any outsole traction pattern.
That leads them to wear down pretty quickly in comparison. So yeah, these are going to last
longer than your standard clog or slide. So for the most part, a lot more similarities between these
two, but the single biggest difference between the clog and the slide is that surprisingly,
the slide has a lot more cushioning than the clogs do. Like this midsole, the stuff that you're
actually walking on is decently thicker than what you find on the clogs. And honestly,
I actually really like it. It's nice to have a decent amount of foam in a pair of slides
underneath your feet. Something that I guess traditional slides don't normally have. They
usually keep it quite thin. Now the sizing, I actually went with my True to Size in both of
these shoes and they fit me perfectly. If you're after either of these, I would recommend, yeah,
just staying with your True to Size. I will mention that the strap going over the top is a little
bit tight, but that's kind of what you want with a pair of slides. You want something that's going to
hold onto your foot so they don't feel like they're just going to slip off. Now actually making a
choice between the two of these, if you're looking at them to like buy one or the other,
it's, it's a little bit more subjective. You know, do you prefer clogs or do you prefer slides?
Both of them are very comfortable and fit very well. And if it comes down to colorways, well,
the slides will also come in a lot of the same really cool colorways that these do. I think the
initial launch has a lot of brighter colors as well as the more muted palettes. I know I really liked
the green, the blue, and the orange that these things came in. So hopefully further down the line,
we'll get some of those colors on these, but enough of this comparison. How did these stack
up to other slides on the market? I've done a bunch of testing of all of the most popular slides out
there. I think some of the top ones that I found were obviously the Yeezy slides. Hoka did a great
job with theirs. Crocs also did a great job. Adidas obviously has the Adelettes, but I think due to the
popularity of the Yeezy slide, that's probably what most people own and what most people are going to
compare these two. So straight away, the Yeezy slides still have softer foam than these. It's
actually pretty crazy that still to this day, I've never found a pair of slides with foam this soft.
It seems like for some reason, Adidas has never really replicated that either. You thought that
they would have, maybe they will in the future. Now one drawback about this foam is that it turns
out it's very grippy or I guess sticky. Like when you're wearing socks with these, which most people
do, and you try and jam your foot inside, it actually pulls the socks down. So it ends up being
super tight around your toes or bunches up at the top over here. So it can end up being a little bit
annoying. And the Nikes don't really feel as bad as the Yeezy slides in that regard. They do feel a
little bit more smooth and silky. So when you put your foot in there, it doesn't really bunch up like
the Yeezy slides do. Now the strap is also a little bit longer on the Yeezy slides, which is something
that I always appreciated about them because it like helps keep your foot in the slide or the slide on
your foot. The Nikes are still pretty long as far as a strap goes. And it does come down quite
away, but there is definitely a little bit more movement on these in comparison to the Yeezy slides.
I guess if we're talking about how well they stay on your foot when you're walking around,
the weight of these is a little bit heavier than these. So I guess that plays into it a little bit
more as well. It's not massive, but that's probably just because of the outsole that they put on here.
It's like increased durability, but increased weight at the same time. Now, interestingly enough,
Yeezy slides have always kind of been known as the chunky bulky slides. However, these are still
thicker, like just comparing the thickness of the footbed that you get on here. The Nike's,
they're pretty chunky and that's a Shaw King W right there. I guess definitely expect that if you
are looking to pick these up, there's clearly a lot of pros and cons between the two softer,
lighter foam, but then also increased risks of completely like smoothing this thing out,
which I have done. Actually, they don't last that long, increased durability, slightly heavier,
and maybe a little bit less soft, still both incredibly comfortable options. But where these two
really separate and where the biggest difference is, is with the price and availability. Like these
Yeezy slides aren't actually available anymore. So if you're someone literally deciding which one
you're going to go with, you're pretty much limited to basically paying resale for this pair of shoes
and buying it either from a reseller or a resale platform. And that means that you're going to be
paying at least double the price for this pair than you would these $60 Nike slides. And if we're
strictly basing all of this off of the comfort, it's pretty close. I would still maybe give the edge
to the Yeezy slides just for that softer cushioned foam, but these Nikes are very,
very comfortable. And with all things considered, I'd probably recommend these over these. Nike
definitely made a really good pair of shoes with, with both of these. And I think it also just makes
perfect sense why these are both so popular. I do think that the demand for, I guess, both of these,
but mainly the slides is only going to go up closer we get to summertime. But obviously I'd love to
know your guys' thoughts down in the comment section. If you tried either of these, which one do you
prefer, the clogs, the slides. If you want to check out another video, there's one right over there. If you want to click that one.
